summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality regressions observed with the latest model variant. Customer shared new failure modes (policy/guardrail misses and hallucinations for claims language). Redwood team proposed scoring tweaks, additional negative examples, and a regression harness. Agreed next steps: share scoring script, run regression tests on extended prompt set, and schedule follow-up security review.
topics: prompt set expansion and negative examples
guardrails and policy enforcement (sensitive PII, hallucination mitigation)
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. um let's do quick roll call then jump into the quality findings.
[00:10] Sara (Silverline): hey all, Sara here. we've got Tom, Priya and Nikhil on. thanks.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): Maya from engineering, I'll cover the regression runs.
[00:30] Tom (Silverline): Tom here.
[00:35] Nikhil (Silverline): Nikhil - product.
[01:10] Ethan: quick agenda - review the new failure modes you reported, talk about scoring changes and thresholds, plan the regression run, and agree next steps. does that align?
[01:22] Sara: yep that's right; biggest concern is a new class of hallucinations where the model invents policy numbers in claim summaries and also misses to redact certain PII.
[01:40] Maya: we saw those too in the sample set you uploaded last week; about 8% of the long-form claim summaries had named entities leaked or invented references.
[01:55] Priya: to be clear, these are not just name leaks - sometimes the model composes "policy 123-45" which is not in our data, so it's hallucinating structured identifiers and that breaks downstream validators.
[02:12] Ethan: right, that aligns with the false positive vs false negative split. we ran a quick diff between v1.2.0 and v1.3.0 of the model, and the delta showed increased permissiveness for generating numeric identifiers.
[02:30] Maya: two root causes: prompt drift (some prompt variants we introduced are less constrained) and a model-variant change where the tokenizer/decoding temperature default was slightly different after quantization.
[02:48] Tom: hmm so is that a quantization artifact? we thought quantized variants would be safe.
[03:00] Maya: it can be, especially when combined with different prompt templates; the runtime's decoding config matters. we can lock decoding params, or push a guardrail in prompt pre-processing that strips personal/identifier patterns.
[03:20] Sara: we need both - we can't rely on only post-hoc filters. regulatory teams want evidence we prevented PII leakage at generation time not just afterwards.
[03:34] Ethan: agreed. on the scoring front we've proposed tightening the precision threshold for identifier detection and adding a specific penalty for hallucinated structured tokens. i'll share the scoring script after the call.
[03:50] Maya: also propose adding negative examples to the prompt set - e.g., example where model must respond with 'insufficient info' or 'refer to human', so the model learns the safe response pattern.
[04:05] Priya: we can provide redacted examples from our corpus; we'll annotate edge cases where false acceptance would be critical.
[04:18] Nikhil: timeline wise, we need to decide by early April whether we go hosted or dedicated for the pilot extension - cost/latency tradeoffs will affect that.
[04:30] Ethan: we did a cost projection - for Silverline's throughput the delta is about 25% cheaper on dedicated for steady throughput, but hosted gives faster onboarding and autoscaling. Carlos will prepare a short comparison.
[04:50] Carlos (Redwood): yeah i'll put together a per-100k token cost/latency table and include breakpoints where dedicated becomes economical.
[05:05] Sara: another ask - can you surface token-level traces? our SREs want to see per-prompt latency heatmaps.
[05:15] Maya: yes, console will show per-route token breakdowns and we can provide sample traces; note sometimes the K-V cache warmup skews the first few latencies.
[05:30] Tom: on security, procurement asked for SOC2 docs and KMS integration details - we had a call with your security brief but need deeper details.
[05:45] Ethan: understood, we'll schedule a security review next week with our security engineer. i'll attach SOC2 report and KMS integration notes.
[06:00] Sara: back to quality, we saw regressions in the scoring dashboard where the accept rate dropped for high-priority prompts; can you explain how delta detection triggers an alert?
[06:15] Maya: current delta detection compares per-prompt Q scores across baselines using a z-score threshold; when mean drops by 2 standard deviations we flag it. however that approach misses systemic guardrail fails, so we're adding rule-based checks for PII and structured token hallucination.
[06:37] Priya: can you incorporate our validators? we run custom regex checks for policy numbers and SSN-like patterns.
[06:45] Maya: yes we can plug that into the regression harness; we'll run the harness with your regex validators as additional gates.
[07:00] Ethan: practical next step - you (Priya) upload the 10k prompt sample with labels, we'll run regression and return a per-prompt report.
[07:12] Priya: I'll do that, aim to have it by Monday.
[07:20] Nikhil: when you run regression, please include the negative test set we discussed in the doc. we added corner cases in tab 'edge-cases'.
[07:35] Maya: copied. also we'll test both hosted and dedicated config profiles; the model variant will be the same but decoding and runtime kernels differ slightly which can change behavior.
[07:52] Tom: what's the plan if regression fails? do we rollback to earlier model?
[08:00] Ethan: fallback policy is to canary back to v1.2.0 for affected routes and open a ticket to remediate the variant. for the POC we can pin to a safer variant until fixes deploy.
[08:15] Sara: ok good. another point - we need to monitor hallucinations around legal language; some outputs looked like invented statute citations.
[08:28] Maya: we'll add a classifier to detect legal-citation patterns and map them to 'untrusted' output. if classifier triggers, response becomes 'refer to human'.
[08:40] Priya: can you tune the classifier thresholds? we're sensitive to false positives because too many referrals will reduce automation value.
[08:50] Ethan: yes that's why we'll produce ROC curves and let you set operating point; we'll suggest a balance that keeps FPR under 2% while catching >90% of hallucinations in our tests.
[09:10] Nikhil: about analytics - will we get per-customer routing logs? we want to validate region/tenant isolation.
[09:20] Carlos: yes for Dedicated we provide tenant-level audit logs and S3 export; hosted has multi-tenant logs but you can ingest filtered artifacts for compliance.
[09:35] Tom: any gotchas around VPC peering and on-prem? we run some parts on-prem and need to confirm network egress.
[09:45] Maya: VPC/private deployment options support peering and private control plane; egress policies can be locked down and we support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[10:00] Sara: ok good. on the scoring details, can you walk through an example of the penalty for hallucinated structured tokens?
[10:10] Maya: sure - we compute token-level novelty relative to trained token histograms; if tokens match structured-ID regex and their joint-probability under the baseline is below threshold, we inject a heavy penalty into the Q score. that pushes the response below acceptance for the gating policy.
[10:32] Priya: will that catch invented dates or numeric IDs?
[10:36] Maya: mostly yes, especially when combined with context-aware checks - e.g., if a token sequence looks like a policy number and there's no preceding reference in the claim, it's suspicious.
[10:50] Ethan: we'll include examples in the scoring script.
[11:00] Sara: is there anything else on the regression harness?
[11:05] Maya: we'll run three passes - baseline, variant, and variant+guardrails. produce per-prompt diff and an aggregate metric set (precision/recall for PII detect, hallucination rate, accept rate).
[11:20] Nikhil: please also include latency percentiles; procurement will ask about p95 under 128 token responses.
[11:30] Carlos: we'll include p50/p95/p99 for each route and for warm vs cold cache.
[11:40] Tom: on price - can you send updated pilot pricing and delta for dedicated?
[11:45] Ethan: yes i'll include pricing options in the follow-up email.
[11:50] Sara: one more item - our compliance team asked for retention settings and ability to purge logs.
[11:58] Maya: retention is configurable; we support short retention for POC and can enable immediate purge endpoints for compliance teams.
[12:10] Priya: ok, we'll prepare a short list of compliance requirements and send tonight.
[12:20] Ethan: great. recap - action items: Ethan share script & pricing, Maya run regression and include validators, Priya upload prompts, Carlos prepare cost/latency deck, schedule security review. anything else?
[12:34] Sara: no that's it. thanks everyone.
[12:38] Ethan: thanks folks, we'll follow up by email and attach the doc links (drive: https://drive.google.com/silverline-poc, sheet: https://redwood.app/poc-results.csv).
[12:50] Tom: thanks. bye.
[12:55] End of meeting
